title: Build the native Codex backend and discovery for accountable sessions
goal: Deliver the first complete native ExecutionBackend by implementing Codex execution, discovery and accountable observations in the new product.
scope: Implement Codex native readiness/discovery and ExecutionBackend against a supported local protocol selected and documented in this task. Preserve native authentication/agent identity, provider version, per-model efforts and requested/sent/reported settings; no previous Codex adapter is credited.

Implement start, bounded output/role response, progress/ToolDenied, cancellation, receipt and native session continuation through the W1-0017 host. Normalize total input/cache-read/cache-write/output/reasoning usage, distinguishing cumulative/resumed counters and Complete/Partial/Unknown coverage.

Expose actual enforceable workspace/capability facts and attributable cessation/never-started observations. Protocol failure, parent exit or disconnect alone cannot release holds; unsupported reattachment remains explicit and cannot cause a duplicate native call.

Build new local protocol fixtures and conformance scenarios through Registry/Gatekeeper/host, plus a documented separately authorized native-run procedure. W3-0001 later adds agent-callable team operations through this native boundary.
context: Authority: model sections 3.1/3.4/3.7/3.9/5.1/5.7, A5/A13 and R-2/R-3/R-8/R-9/R-19/R-20; greenfield baseline 0c61ff1.

Proposed modules: crates/ymp-runtime/src/backends/codex.rs and focused protocol/discovery/usage modules, with new runtime protocol fixtures. W1-0003 supplies Registry/offerings and W1-0017 the execution host; create the actual adapter here rather than assuming App Server or another prior implementation is delivered.

Choose the native wire protocol using installed/official provider information during implementation. Do not copy credentials, infer unsupported model/effort values or rely on old tests. Fixture evidence is separate from real inference; builds/tests do not authorize native calls or real user-data mutation.
acceptance: Through the real Registry/Gatekeeper/host consumer, a new Codex protocol fixture discovers supported offerings, runs a bounded admitted turn, returns attributable role output and settles a correctly normalized receipt without copying authentication.

Unsupported settings, malformed/foreign responses, duplicate/partial/cumulative usage and ambiguous cancellation/reconnect cases are denied or recorded truthfully; none grants authority, duplicates a start or releases unresolved holds.

Codex and Scripted run the shared execution contract through actual consumers. Native-run evidence, if separately authorized and collected, records exact runtime version/settings/observations and is not conflated with fixture behavior.
